Fit the calibration model

Source: R/calibrate.R
fit_calibration.Rd

Fits a calibration model to all the reviewed clips. The species and site levels of validations are stored with the model, so that score_detections() can score new detections.

Usage

fit_calibration(
  validations,
  formula,
  engine = c("lme4", "brms"),
  prior = NULL,
  control = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

validations

A data frame (or tibble) returned by read_validations(), one row per reviewed clip.

formula

A model formula, usually the best one of compare_calibration_models().

engine

Character scalar, one of "lme4" (default) or "brms".

prior

NULL or a brmsprior object. With engine = "brms", the prior, e.g. from calibration_prior(). Required.

control

NULL or a single object with settings of the fitting algorithm: a lme4::glmerControl() object (formula with random effects) or a list of stats::glm.control() arguments (formula without them) with engine = "lme4"; a list of sampler settings passed to brms::brm() with engine = "brms". NULL (default) keeps the settings described in "Maximum likelihood fit" and the 'brms' defaults. See the section "Maximum likelihood fit".

...

engine = "brms": further arguments for brms::brm() (e.g. chains, iter, cores, backend, seed). Without seed, one is drawn from R's random number generator (so set.seed() before the call makes the fit reproducible) and passed to brms::brm().

Value

A glm, glmerMod or brmsfit model, with the attribute sheepdog_levels (the species and site levels), used by score_detections() and plot_calibration(). A brmsfit also carries the attribute sheepdog_seed, the seed given to Stan, so that the fit can be repeated.

Details

With engine = "lme4" (default), the model is fitted by maximum likelihood ('lme4' for random effects, glm() otherwise). A model with random effects whose fit is singular (a variance estimated at zero or a correlation at +-1) raises a warning: the fixed effects and the predictions can still be used, but the variance components on the boundary should not be interpreted, and a simpler model may predict as well. Check them with lme4::VarCorr(). The other messages of lme4::glmer() are passed on, prefixed by lme4:, and every message of the fit is kept in the attribute sheepdog_messages of the model (convergence warnings of 'lme4' are warnings and are passed on as such).

With engine = "brms", the model is fitted in a Bayesian framework with 'brms' (Bernoulli family, logit link). The prior must be given explicitly; calibration_prior() builds an example centred on an already calibrated score. After the fit, calibration_diagnostics() runs and a warning is raised when R-hat, the effective sample sizes or the divergent transitions fail the usual limits. Check the prior with prior_predictive_calibration(), the fit with brms::pp_check() and the sensitivity to the prior with calibration_sensitivity().

Formula and model matrix

The formula uses the syntax of 'lme4' for random effects ((term | group)) and is turned into model matrices by the fitting function itself: stats::glm() for a formula without random effects, lme4::glmer() otherwise, or brms::brm(). sheepdog does not build the matrices. The response is tp (1 = true positive, 0 = false positive) and the predictor of the score is logit_conf, the logit of the BirdNET confidence bounded at 1e-4 and 1 - 1e-4 (see read_validations()); the inverse transform, from the linear predictor to P(TP), is stats::plogis(). Only the columns named in the formula enter the model: the other columns of validations (for example those kept with keep in read_validations()) are neither used nor stored in the fitted object. The species and site levels are stored in the attribute sheepdog_levels.

Input checks and missing values

validations must be a data frame (a tibble, data.frame or data.table; it is converted to a tibble) with the columns site and species (factors or character vectors; ordered factors are used as unordered), tp (0/1, or logical) and every variable of formula, usually logit_conf (numeric, without NaN or infinite values; extra classes such as 'units' are dropped). The response of formula must be tp. Rows with a missing value in a variable of the formula are left out with a message; this policy is fixed, the same in both engines, and no missing value reaches the fitting function. Before the fit, an error is raised when all the clips have the same verdict or when the fixed effects are collinear (rank-deficient model matrix), a warning when the verdicts are completely separated by the score (the maximum likelihood slope is then infinite), and a message lists species with a single verdict class or separated verdicts. With engine = "brms", prior must be a brmsprior object.

Maximum likelihood fit

Models with random effects are fitted by lme4::glmer() with lme4::glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 1e5)): the bound optimisation by quadratic approximation, with up to 100000 function evaluations, a larger budget than the 'lme4' default, for the correlated random slopes of the larger calibration models. The convergence tolerances are those of 'lme4' unless control is given; convergence warnings of 'lme4' are passed on. Models without random effects use the iteratively reweighted least squares of stats::glm(), with the default stats::glm.control() (epsilon = 1e-8, maxit = 25) unless control is given.

control replaces these settings: a lme4::glmerControl() object for a formula with random effects (for example another optimiser, a larger optCtrl = list(maxfun = ) or other check.conv.grad tolerances), or a list of stats::glm.control() arguments (epsilon, maxit) for a formula without them. With engine = "brms", control is passed to brms::brm() as its list of sampler settings (for example list(adapt_delta = 0.95, max_treedepth = 12)).

Bayesian computation

With engine = "brms", the posterior is sampled with the No-U-Turn Sampler (NUTS) of Stan (Carpenter et al. 2017, doi:10.18637/jss.v076.i01 ) through 'brms' (Bürkner 2017, doi:10.18637/jss.v080.i01 ). The computational settings are those of brms::brm() unless they are given in ...: 4 chains of 2000 iterations each, of which the first half (warmup = floor(iter / 2)) is warmup, without thinning (thin = 1), and random initial values (init = NULL). Initial values can be set with init, passed on to brms::brm(); to start from a previous fit, pass its posterior means as init or refit the model. stats::update() on the returned brmsfit runs the sampler again but returns an object without the attributes sheepdog_levels and sheepdog_seed, so a model refitted that way cannot be passed to score_detections(); call fit_calibration() again instead.

Only NUTS is supported. Other algorithms of brms::brm() (algorithm = "meanfield", for instance) can be passed through ..., but calibration_diagnostics(), which reads the NUTS parameters, then fails. The convergence checks of calibration_diagnostics() always run after the fit and cannot be switched off; a model that fails them raises a warning, which suppressWarnings() silences. sheepdog has no verbosity argument of its own: the progress output of Stan is controlled by refresh (e.g. refresh = 0, passed on to the Stan backend) and silent (e.g. silent = 2) of brms::brm(), and the messages of sheepdog by suppressMessages().

Methods for the fitted model

The returned object keeps the class of the fitting function, so the methods of stats, 'lme4' and 'brms' apply. Confidence intervals of the coefficients come from stats::confint() for glm and glmerMod models (profile likelihood by default; method = "Wald" for a faster approximation of a glmerMod), and credible intervals from brms::posterior_interval() or summary() for a brmsfit. stats::residuals() returns deviance residuals for glm and glmerMod models and, for a brmsfit, the posterior summary of the response residuals (observed minus fitted probability). With a binary response, residuals take two values for each fitted probability and say little one by one; check the fit with the calibration intercept and slope of compare_calibration_models(), with calibration_quality(), or with the binned posterior predictive check of calibration_ppc() for a brmsfit.

Examples

ex <- system.file("extdata", "example", package = "sheepdog")
val <- read_validations(list.files(file.path(ex, "validation"),
                                   full.names = TRUE))
#> 2467 reviewed clips (1577 TP / 890 FP) of 8 species at 4 sites.
# Maximum likelihood, one species-level random intercept
if (requireNamespace("lme4", quietly = TRUE)) {
  fit <- fit_calibration(val, tp ~ logit_conf + (1 | species))
  print(lme4::fixef(fit))
  confint(fit, method = "Wald", parm = "beta_")
}
#> (Intercept)  logit_conf 
#>  -0.2060523   1.6030183 
#>                  2.5 %    97.5 %
#> (Intercept) -0.9305499 0.5184454
#> logit_conf   1.4584248 1.7476119
if (FALSE) { # interactive() && requireNamespace("brms", quietly = TRUE)
# Bayesian fit: the prior is always given explicitly. Fitting compiles a
# Stan model, which takes minutes, so this part runs only interactively.
f <- tp ~ logit_conf + (1 | species)
prior <- calibration_prior(f, val)
fit_b <- fit_calibration(val, f, engine = "brms", prior = prior,
                         chains = 4, iter = 2000, seed = 1,
                         refresh = 0)
calibration_diagnostics(fit_b)
brms::posterior_interval(fit_b)
}
